- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤ -0.33) in recent days, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes; apply a 1–3 day lag correction: if price spikes, forecast should dip slightly in next 2–3 periods.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is > 2σ above recent 18-day mean, reduce by 1–2% per period until convergence.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: if sentiment drops below 0.33 after 10–15 days, reduce forecast slope by 10–15%.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses late-period momentum; add a 1–2% upward bias if sentiment remains positive after day 20–25.
